texts.error.no_room_for_buffers: There is no room in the core's memory for the picture or the sound.
texts.error.start_failed: QUASI88 could not start the machine. Check that the firmware is there.
texts.firmware.2608_bd_wav.about: One of the six drum recordings of the YM2608 sound chip, as the WAV files PC-88 and PC-98 emulators share (2608_BD.WAV). Used for the drums of Sound Board II when the Sound Generator is fmgen.
texts.firmware.2608_hh_wav.about: One of the six drum recordings of the YM2608 sound chip, as the WAV files PC-88 and PC-98 emulators share (2608_HH.WAV). Used for the drums of Sound Board II when the Sound Generator is fmgen.
texts.firmware.2608_rim_wav.about: One of the six drum recordings of the YM2608 sound chip, as the WAV files PC-88 and PC-98 emulators share (2608_RIM.WAV). Used for the drums of Sound Board II when the Sound Generator is fmgen.
texts.firmware.2608_sd_wav.about: One of the six drum recordings of the YM2608 sound chip, as the WAV files PC-88 and PC-98 emulators share (2608_SD.WAV). Used for the drums of Sound Board II when the Sound Generator is fmgen.
texts.firmware.2608_tom_wav.about: One of the six drum recordings of the YM2608 sound chip, as the WAV files PC-88 and PC-98 emulators share (2608_TOM.WAV). Used for the drums of Sound Board II when the Sound Generator is fmgen.
texts.firmware.2608_top_wav.about: One of the six drum recordings of the YM2608 sound chip, as the WAV files PC-88 and PC-98 emulators share (2608_TOP.WAV). Used for the drums of Sound Board II when the Sound Generator is fmgen.
texts.firmware.disk_rom.about: The ROM of the floppy disk unit's own CPU (DISK.ROM or N88SUB.ROM, 2 or 8 KiB).
texts.firmware.kanji1_rom.about: The level 1 kanji ROM (128 KiB, KANJI1.ROM or N88KNJ1.ROM). The machine's text font is taken from it too.
texts.firmware.kanji2_rom.about: The level 2 kanji ROM (128 KiB, KANJI2.ROM or N88KNJ2.ROM).
texts.firmware.n88_0_rom.about: The first of the four 8 KiB banks of N88-BASIC V2's fourth ROM (N88_0.ROM or N88EXT0.ROM).
texts.firmware.n88_1_rom.about: The second of the four 8 KiB banks of N88-BASIC V2's fourth ROM (N88_1.ROM or N88EXT1.ROM).
texts.firmware.n88_2_rom.about: The third of the four 8 KiB banks of N88-BASIC V2's fourth ROM (N88_2.ROM or N88EXT2.ROM).
texts.firmware.n88_3_rom.about: The fourth of the four 8 KiB banks of N88-BASIC V2's fourth ROM (N88_3.ROM or N88EXT3.ROM).
texts.firmware.n88_rom.about: The main ROM of a PC-8801mkIISR or later that you own: N88-BASIC (32 KiB, N88.ROM).
texts.firmware.n88jisho_rom.about: The dictionary ROM of the later models (512 KiB, N88JISHO.ROM or JISYO.ROM).
texts.firmware.n88n_rom.about: The N-BASIC ROM of the same machine (32 KiB, N88N.ROM or N80.ROM), for the N mode.
texts.firmware.pc88_rom.about: The BASIC and disk unit ROMs of one PC-8801mkIISR or later that you own, in the one file M88 and QUASI88 read (PC88.ROM, 88 KiB): N88-BASIC, its four extension banks, the top of N-BASIC and the disk unit's ROM. A dump with the whole of N-BASIC (112 KiB) also runs the N mode.
texts.firmware.ym2608_adpcm_rom_bin.about: The drum ROM inside the YM2608 sound chip, as MAME dumps it (8 KiB, in MAME's ym2608.zip). Used for the drums of Sound Board II when the Sound Generator is MAME.
texts.setting.basic_mode.about: The mode the machine starts in, as the mode switch on the front of a PC-8801 sets it. V2 is N88-BASIC V2, the mode almost every game is written for and the default. V1H and V1S are the older N88-BASIC V1 in its fast and standard speeds, and N is N-BASIC, the PC-8001 compatible mode a few early games need. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.boot_from.about: Whether the machine starts from the floppy disk in drive 1 (the default) or straight into BASIC in ROM. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.cpu_clock.about: The speed of the main CPU. 4MHz is the PC-8801mkIISR's, and the default; 8MHz is the fast mode of the FR, MR and later models. Most games are written for 4 MHz, and some run too fast at 8 MHz. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.cpu_timing.about: How QUASI88 runs the main CPU and the disk unit's CPU together (its -cpu option). 0, the default, runs the disk unit's CPU only while the main CPU waits for it, the fastest. 1 runs them side by side while they talk to each other, and 2 runs them in turns of 5 microseconds all the time, the slowest and the closest to a real machine. A few games need 1 or 2 to load. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.dictionary_rom.about: Whether the machine has the dictionary ROM (N88JISHO.ROM) of the later models, used by their kana to kanji conversion. Off by default. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.dip_switches.about: The machine's DIP switches, as four hexadecimal digits (QUASI88's -dipsw). The default, 391A, is QUASI88's. They set the terminal mode, the number of text lines and columns and the serial line. A value that is not hexadecimal is refused, and the default is used. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.extra_ram.about: How many 128 KB extended RAM cards are fitted. The default is none. A few programs use them. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.fdc_wait.about: Makes the floppy disk controller take as long as a real one to move the head and wait for the sector to come round (QUASI88's -fdc_wait). On by default, so games load in about the time they take on a real PC-8801. Off, the controller answers almost at once and games load sooner (up to about 2 seconds in the games tried), but that is not as accurate to real hardware. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.kanji_level2.about: Whether the machine has the level 2 kanji ROM (KANJI2.ROM), which holds the less common kanji. Off by default; without it those kanji show as blanks. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.lua_memory_events.about: Lets Lua scripts stop at memory either Z80 runs, reads or writes (event.on_bus_exec, on_bus_read and on_bus_write), by the address the CPU uses (scope Main CPU or Sub CPU), and change the values read or written. It uses a copy of QUASI88 that checks every instruction and memory access, a little slower, so it is off by default. The machine runs the same either way, so a movie plays back the same with any value. Takes effect when the machine starts.
texts.setting.memory_wait.about: Slows the CPU down by the wait states a real PC-8801's memory adds (QUASI88's -mem_wait). Off by default, as in QUASI88. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.monitor.about: Which monitor the machine is told is connected. 24kHz, the default, is the high resolution monitor that shows the 640x400 modes; 15kHz is a TV-like monitor, on which the machine shows 200 lines only. Some games check it. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.port.about: What is plugged into the sound board's controller port: a joystick (the default), a mouse, or nothing. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.rhythm_samples.about: Whether the drums of the YM2608 (Sound Board II) play. They are recordings that no ROM of the PC-8801 holds: with the MAME Sound Generator they come from the YM2608's drum ROM as MAME dumps it (ym2608_adpcm_rom.bin, 8 KiB), with fmgen from the six 2608_*.WAV files PC-88 and PC-98 emulators share. Off by default, as the drums are then silent, which needs no file. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.rom_files.about: Where the BASIC and disk unit ROMs come from. PC88.ROM, the default, is the one file that M88 and QUASI88 read, holding all of them from one machine. Separate files are QUASI88's N88.ROM, N88_0.ROM to N88_3.ROM, N88N.ROM and DISK.ROM. The files of one set must all come from the same model: a mixed set starts, but games then show garbage or do not start. The kanji ROMs are separate files either way. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.sound_board.about: Which sound chip the machine has. Sound Board I is the YM2203 (OPN) of the PC-8801mkIISR, and the default. Sound Board II is the YM2608 (OPNA) of the later models and of the sound board II, with stereo, rhythm and ADPCM sound; games that support it say so. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.sound_generator.about: Which code makes the sound of the FM chip. MAME is the YM2203 and YM2608 emulation QUASI88 takes from MAME, and QUASI88's default; fmgen is cisc's FM sound generator, which many prefer for the YM2608. The chip's timers are QUASI88's own either way. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.start_time.about: The date and time the machine's calendar clock shows when it is switched on, exactly as written here: the clock holds a local time and has no time zone. The default is 1988-01-01 00:00:00. The clock then runs with the emulated time, not with the time on your computer. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.volume_a_d_p_c_m.about: The ADPCM samples of the YM2608 (Sound Board II), in per cent. The default, 100, is QUASI88's. Only the sound changes, never what the machine does, so a movie plays back the same with any value.
texts.setting.volume_beep.about: The machine's beeper, in per cent. The default, 60, is QUASI88's. Only the sound changes, never what the machine does, so a movie plays back the same with any value.
texts.setting.volume_f_m.about: The FM music of the sound chip, in per cent. The default, 100, is QUASI88's. Only the sound changes, never what the machine does, so a movie plays back the same with any value.
texts.setting.volume_fmgen.about: The whole sound chip when the Sound Generator is fmgen, in per cent. The default, 100, is QUASI88's. Only the sound changes, never what the machine does, so a movie plays back the same with any value.
texts.setting.volume_rhythm.about: The drums of the YM2608 (Sound Board II), in per cent. The default, 100, is QUASI88's. Only the sound changes, never what the machine does, so a movie plays back the same with any value.
texts.setting.volume_s_s_g.about: The SSG part of the sound chip, which most games use for sound effects, in per cent. The default, 20, is QUASI88's. Only the sound changes, never what the machine does, so a movie plays back the same with any value.
texts.slot.floppy.help: Floppy disk images in the D88 format (.d88, .88d). A D88 file may hold several disks. The first disk of the first file is in drive 1 when the machine starts, and the second file, or the first file's second disk, in drive 2. The order here is the order the Previous, Next and Swap Floppy Disk inputs go through, every disk of each file in turn. What the machine writes to a disk stays for the session and can be exported as save data.
texts.slot.tape.help: Cassette tape images (.t88, or QUASI88's raw .cmt). The first is in the data recorder when the machine starts; the Tape Previous, Next, Swap and Eject inputs change it, in the order listed here, and Tape Rewind winds it back to the start. A game on tape is loaded from BASIC (for example with LOAD or CLOAD, or MON and L). What the machine saves to tape goes into tape-save.cmt, which can be exported as save data.
